subject: Throughput assurance: measurement playbook, latency targets & commercial ask
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orchardai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@orchardai.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated throughput warranty — initial ask

Rachel — thanks again for the demo. Before we get to a PO, procurement and engineering need a clear, testable throughput/latency guarantee for the Dedicated GPU pool that will host our API. High level asks: what tokens/sec guarantee can you commit for our baseline model (open-7B-quant) at p50/p95 latencies, and how do you measure it? Also want to understand commercial remedies (credits or discounts) if you miss the target during acceptance or production.

Can you send a short playbook we can share with procurement/eng?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, OrchardAI

---
Attachments: none

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orchardai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty — initial ask

Alex — appreciate the clear list. Summary below and attaching a short runbook (see attachment) that outlines the exact measurement steps, assumptions, and the commercial fallback we propose. High-level overview first: 

- Commitment we can offer for your baseline open-7B-quant (seen in your test corpus): 120k tokens/sec sustained per reserved GPU pool slab (definition below) with p50 latency <= 85ms and p95 latency <= 210ms on the sequence-length mix you provided (p50=128, p95=512). These numbers assume the "medium" batching profile (auto-batching enabled up to 16 requests).

- Measurement methodology: 10 minute warm-up, 30 minute steady-state window, traffic shaped to match your sequence-length distribution and request concurrency. We use real tokenization with your prompt set (no synthetic truncation) and require you to provide 5 representative prompt buckets (we'll run each). Acceptable measurement variance: +/-5%.

- Remediation/commercials: If the observed tokens/sec or latencies are outside the guaranteed range during acceptance, we offer either (a) pro-rated usage credits equal to one week of committed capacity for that slab, or (b) a one-time 10% discount on the first 3 months of invoices for the affected slab — choose which you prefer. For continued misses in production, we propose a rolling credit equal to 2x the difference for the first month while we remediate.

I've attached the runbook and a sample log format. Karthik/Ben — please see the measurement details below and flag any changes to the technical assumptions.

- Rachel
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-validation-runbook.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orchardai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty — initial ask

Alex — quick technical clarifications to make sure the test is apples-to-apples: 

1) Model variant: we will run the benchmark on open-7B-quant (INT8). If you plan to use a different quant or a tuned variant, please flag it now.
2) Sequence distribution: your provided p50=128 / p95=512 — is that for prompt+response combined? We need the tokenization script you use (or sample prompts) so our harness reproduces real subtoken counts.
3) Concurrency pattern: are you sending steady concurrent requests (e.g., 32 concurrent streams) or a bursty pattern? Our acceptance window requires a steady ramp to target concurrency; if you use bursty traffic, please include that scenario as an alternate test.
4) Environment: acceptance runs will be scheduled in your Dedicated pool with no other tenants. We will pin the pool to the GPU family you requested.

If those align, we'll schedule a formal acceptance run next week and produce the measurement artifacts (traces, aggregate tokens/sec, latency CDFs, and per-request KV cache hit rates).

Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Quoted text: "Rachel — appreciate the clear list..."

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orchardai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@orchardai.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty — initial ask

Thanks — answers inline:
- Model variant: yes, we'll run open-7B-quant in INT8 as delivered.
- Sequence distribution: combined prompt+response — I'll upload a tokenized sample set and the tokenization script. Expect ~70% short prompts (<64) and a long-tail up to 512 (your p95).
- Concurrency: steady-state for acceptance: 48 concurrent streams. Production will be bursty, but acceptance should be steady to validate baseline.
- Environment: agreed, isolated Dedicated slab.

Procurement: we're comfortable with the proposed credit remedy provided Redwood will also agree to a runbook-based acceptance and share the raw logs/traces. Can you confirm how long Redwood will retain the logs and the format?

Alex

Quoted text: "1) Model variant..."

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orchardai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty — initial ask

Alex / team — quick commercial note. Given the 48-concurrency steady-state target and the sequence mix you described, the commitment maps to a 3-slab reserved pool (we define a slab as a predictable GPU allocation unit for your commit). Pricing impact: standard reserved-commit discount tiers apply — with a 12-month commit we can offer a 20% discount; with a 24-month commit we can move to 28%. If OrchardAI prefers a shorter 6-month pilot, discount drops to 12% and we add a one-time setup fee to cover acceptance run engineer hours.

Regarding logs/retention: we will provide the raw aggregated benchmark logs and per-request traces in the agreed format (JSONL) for the acceptance run and retain them for 90 days. For production, log retention follows the contract tier (90/365 options) — we'll include that clause in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
- Rachel: share the attached runbook and the benchmark harness repo link.
- Alex: upload the tokenized sample set and confirm which commercial option you prefer (6/12/24 months).
- We'll schedule a 60-minute acceptance window and a dry-run 48h before the live acceptance.

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
